us_large_broad.rationale: Facts: Q3 S&P 500 blended EPS growth is 31.4% (84% beat, but the average beat was only 2.7%), and the forward P/E has compressed to 17.7 (FactSet). On Nov 5 the S&P fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq 5.5%, entering a correction on post-midterm data-centre restriction fears plus Microsoft trimming Oracle and neocloud capacity and Oracle's $20B raise at 7-8.65% coupons. Interpretation: the cap-weighted index carries the shared AI-capex/funding factor, while a December hike is about 75% priced and Nov 10 CPI, Nov 17 Nvidia and the Dec 11 funding deadline cluster ahead. Equal-weight RSP hit a record on Nov 4, so breadth is healthy and the drawdown is concentrated: -1, not -2. This is the same risk as tech_ai_semis and should not be counted separately.

McDonald's raised its dividend 4% and Lam Research authorized a $25B buyback. Michigan 1-year inflation expectations eased to 4.3% and gasoline is down 33c in a month, supporting staples margins. Interpretation: defensive/quality leadership is a coordinated factor rotation out of AI momentum. It is +1, not +2, because these are price facts more than catalysts, prices are already 2-3% off the Nov 4 highs, the 10y is near 4.86% with hike risk, and high-yield variants (VYM, DVY) lag. Shares a driver with healthcare_biotech +1; do not double count.

Earnings were mixed: McDonald's US comps -0.2%, Airbnb beat, DraftKings missed. Interpretation: falling fuel costs and jobs are a tailwind, but they are part of the oil-unwind trade that reverses on any Iran strike (FGE window mid-Nov to mid-Dec). Diesel stays tight, XLY is -1% YTD, and HD/TGT/WMT report Nov 17-19. Net neutral with an upside tilt.

Facts: BDC Q3 non-accruals at cost are elevated (ARCC 2.4%, OBDC 2.9%, BXSL 2.8%, FSK 6.4%), NII is falling, and BXSL declared a $0.60 March dividend vs $0.77. AIG beat but carried catastrophe losses. Interpretation: lender equity has not priced AI contagion and exposure looks dispersed. Slow private-credit erosion, Democratic oversight from 2027 and the CoreWeave/Nebius prints offset this, so neutral. Correction: falling BDC NII reflects spread compression, not Fed cuts (the Fed hiked in September).

regime_notes: One AI-capex/funding factor drove the week. The midterm data-centre backlash, Microsoft's Oracle/neocloud pullback and Oracle's expensive $20B raise produced the Nov 5 rout (S&P -4.4%, Nasdaq -5.5%, IWM -4.6%, HY +16bp). Fundamentals stayed strong: Q3 EPS +31.4%, Nvidia guided $108B, TSMC Q4 +14% q/q. So the cap-weighted drawdown reads as multiple compression and financing stress rather than demand collapse, and mean reversion is the base case. Leadership rotated hard into defensive, quality, dividend and equal-weight (all at records on Nov 4), which should be treated as one factor bet. The oil-premium unwind (Brent about $118 futures to about $98) helps consumers and inflation expectations but reverses on any Iran strike decision. The Fed is hiking, not cutting: a Dec 9 hike is about 75% priced and Oct CPI on Nov 10 (Cleveland core nowcast 0.21%) is the key swing factor.

red_flags.issue: BXSL declared $0.60 for the March 2027 record date vs a $0.77 run-rate (about -22%), with Q4 only 88% NII-covered. OBDC's base dividend is down to $0.31 from $0.37. BDC income ETF yields likely reset lower.
Concentration risk: cap-weighted indices carry the AI-capex factor (QQQ -6.5%, VOO -4.4% on Nov 5) while equal-weight RSP set a record. No fund event, but prefer equal-weight within the bucket.
